# Draft:Jalaun District in the Indian Rebellion of 1857

----
References
Pathans of Kalpi and Sarawan in the Indian Rebellion of 1857
The Indian Rebellion of 1857 was a major uprising against the rule of the British East India Company in northern and central India. The town of Kalpi in present-day Jalaun district, Uttar Pradesh, was an important center of rebel activity during 1857–1858.
Kalpi as a Rebel Center
During the rebellion, Kalpi became a base for rebel leaders such as Rani Lakshmibai, Tatya Tope, and Nana Sahib. After the fall of Jhansi in 1858, rebel forces regrouped at Kalpi and continued their resistance against British forces.
Pathans of Sarawan and Kalpi
According to local oral traditions and regional history of Jalaun district, Pathan families from Kalpi and nearby village Sarawan participated in the local resistance movements during the Indian Rebellion of 1857. They joined rebel groups and supported the resistance against British forces in the region.
Lohagarh Fight
Local historical accounts in the Kalpi–Jalaun region mention a conflict remembered as the Lohagarh fight, in which local fighters, including Pathans from Kalpi and Sarawan, fought against British forces. While detailed documentation of this battle is limited in major historical records, it is remembered in local tradition as part of the wider resistance movement in Bundelkhand during 1857.
Legacy
The bravery of local fighters from Kalpi and Sarawan is remembered in local history and oral traditions of Jalaun district. These stories form part of the cultural and historical heritage of the region.
